findings.title: Queries are interpolated twice in the shard path
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery now interpolates each target with applyTemplateVariables. It then passes the already-interpolated targets, via runSplitQuery at line 163, into code that applies applyTemplateVariables to each target again. Double interpolation can corrupt values that contain `$` or escaped characters after the first pass, and it duplicates ad-hoc filter injection. Adhoc filters may be added twice to the expression. It also costs extra work for every shard sub-request. The test change that expects applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times shows the repeated calls. Interpolate once at the top level and skip it in the inner runSplitQuery, for example with an option.

findings.title: applyTemplateVariables may mutate the original request targets
findings.body: The map result replaces the targets, but the tests' mocks of applyTemplateVariables mutate and return the input query. If the real implementation returns shared objects, request.targets gets modified. Later retries and sub-requests would then see interpolated expressions. trackGroupedQueries receives the original request, which could end up inconsistent. Callers may also depend on the un-interpolated targets.

findings.title: Assertion on call count 5 is brittle and encodes the double interpolation
findings.body: toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5) hard-codes the number of redundant applyTemplateVariables calls (1 outer, then 4 inner, one per sub-request). It makes the double interpolation look intentional, and it will break when the group sizing changes.
